eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from meteorological agencies and models place Lucknow’s August 20 maximum near 33–34 °C amid typical late-monsoon conditions of high humidity, scattered thundershowers, and moderate southwesterly flow. These conditions limit strong daytime heating yet allow brief clear spells that can push readings into the low-to-mid 30s. Updated guidance expected later today from the India Meteorological Department will refine steering patterns and convective timing, the key variables that could shift the realized high by 1–2 °C and move the implied probabilities accordingly.

Historical August normals hover around 89–91°F, but the recent heat anomaly and lack of strong steering winds keep the upper end of the distribution in play if storms develop later than modeled.

Recent conditions reinforce this: August 2026 has featured variable but moderated highs (recent downtown readings in the upper 80s to low 90s), with no strong offshore winds or heat dome to push extremes. Sunny skies are expected, yet the typical August marine layer keeps afternoon temperatures from climbing sharply at official monitoring sites. Historical August averages hover around 77°F, and current forecasts align closely with the market’s leading 80–81°F bin (52.5% implied probability), followed by 78–79°F.

Traders appear to weigh the high likelihood of stable marine moderation against any last-minute clearing that could add a degree or two, explaining the tight clustering around 80°F with lower odds on outliers above 84°F. Updated NWS or NOAA guidance on afternoon wind shifts or cloud cover will be the key near-term driver.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) and national meteorological services consistently project Moscow’s daytime maximum on August 21 near 21–23 °C.** This narrow range underpins the market’s concentration of implied probability on 22 °C (45 %) and 23 °C (30.5 %), with 21 °C next at 17 %.

August climatology in Moscow features average highs of roughly 20–22 °C and modest day-to-day variability under typical late-summer high-pressure influence. Current model runs show no strong frontal systems, significant moisture advection, or rapid temperature advection that would push the maximum outside this band. Light winds and mostly cloudy to partly cloudy conditions are expected to limit both strong daytime heating and rapid cooling, keeping the peak tightly constrained.

With the event less than 24 hours away, the latest short-range guidance exhibits high agreement, limiting upside or downside risk and explaining why outcomes above 24 °C or below 21 °C carry single-digit or lower implied probabilities. Any last-minute model shift in cloud cover, wind direction, or boundary-layer moisture could nudge the realized high by 1 °C, but the current consensus leaves little room for larger deviations.
